title: 🤖 A military robotics company with no salaries and no health insurance! Foundation employees without income for a third month!
body: 🤖 A military robotics company with no salaries and no health insurance! Foundation employees without income for a third month!

Foundation Future Industries, maker of humanoid robots for military and industrial purposes, told its employees in an evening message on Friday that their health insurance through Rippling had been canceled retroactively to October, in a new chapter of its escalating financial crisis, according to reports revealed on November 22.

The company told employees it would offer them temporary coverage for November and reimburse its premiums, blaming the benefits management company — but Rippling replied that a client unable to meet payroll and benefits obligations for several months is first warned, then its contract is terminated, suggesting the cancellation was due to non-payment, not an administrative error.

Employees have received no salary since October 15, after the company missed the October 30 payday, and with the November 30 payday approaching, workers face a third consecutive pay cycle with no income, while many are draining their savings to cover living expenses, and some new hires have not received a full salary since joining the company.

Since August, the company has been seeking a short-term rescue loan from three or four investment firms, including its current investor Tribe Capital, to keep it alive until a possible $150 million investment from South Korea's Bace group, which could arrive in December or January but has not yet been finalized.

The crisis is complicated by the fact that CEO and co-founder Sankaet Pathak had borrowed $4.6 million from the company last year — a loan that angered employees — while the company was founded in 2024, is backed by prominent figures, and aims to deploy its humanoid robots in conflict zones and industrial sites.

The company's HR staff warned employees against turning to California authorities to recover their wages, saying anyone who complains will be fired, while many employees are looking for other jobs and attendance at the company's San Francisco headquarters has dropped sharply.
Simply put: a company building robots for wars cannot pay its employees' salaries or their health insurance... will a new investment save it before it collapses?
Do you believe the promises of big startups after a story like this, or is caution a must before joining any of them?
